# QUBT Technical Analysis Report — 2026-10-09

## Executive Summary

QUBT (Quantum Computing Inc.) closed at **$7.44** on 2026-10-09 (open $7.57, high $7.57, low $7.34, volume ~5.0M). The stock is in a **confirmed downtrend across all timeframes**: price sits below the 10 EMA ($7.94), 50 SMA ($8.42), and 200 SMA ($9.10), with a fully bearish moving-average stack. Momentum has deteriorated sharply over the past three weeks — a mid-September rally to ~$9.16 has fully unwound, and the stock is now near its recent lows. RSI at 32.6 is approaching oversold territory but not yet below 30. The short-term setup is bearish with emerging capitulation characteristics; the medium-term trend offers no structural support until at least the $8.40–$8.50 zone.

## Indicator Selection Rationale

I selected 8 complementary indicators covering trend, momentum, volatility, and mean-reversion:

- **close_10_ema, close_50_sma, close_200_sma** — fast/medium/long trend stack for direction and dynamic support/resistance.
- **macd + macdh** — momentum direction and the rate of change of momentum (early divergence signal).
- **rsi** — overbought/oversold condition.
- **boll (+ boll_ub/boll_lb via verified snapshot)** — mean-reversion context and band positioning.
- **atr** — volatility regime for stop sizing.

I skipped vwma (volume data already shows declining participation; VWMA adds little over the SMA stack) and macds (redundant with macd/macdh pair).

## Trend Analysis

**Long-term (200 SMA):** The 200 SMA at $9.10 has been declining steadily from $9.47 on 2026-09-09 — the long-term trend is clearly down. Price at $7.44 trades ~18% below it, confirming a bear market structure. There is no golden-cross setup; the stock has been in a persistent downtrend since the data window began (it fell from ~$21 in October 2025 to ~$7.44 now, roughly -65% over 12 months).

**Medium-term (50 SMA):** The 50 SMA at $8.42 turned up briefly during the September rally but has flattened and begun rolling over ($8.43 on 10/08 → $8.42 on 10/09). Price is ~12% below it. The September high of $9.16 (2026-09-24) never even challenged the 200 SMA — the rally was a bear-market bounce, and it has now failed.

**Short-term (10 EMA):** The 10 EMA at $7.94 is falling steeply and price has been below it since 10/05. The last five closes ($8.18 → $7.94 → $7.86 → $7.62 → $7.45 → $7.44) show accelerating downside with consecutive lower lows. No bullish crossover is near.

## Momentum

- **MACD (-0.21) / Histogram (-0.14):** MACD crossed back below zero on 10/06 after a brief positive stretch during the September rally, and the histogram has been negative and expanding since 10/01. Momentum is negative and still worsening — no divergence yet visible in the MACD series; each price low is matched by a lower MACD reading.
- **RSI (32.6):** Down from 62.8 on 09/24. RSI is approaching the 30 oversold threshold but has not reached it. Notably, RSI has fallen faster than price in the last week, suggesting sellers remain in control. A break below 30 could mark capitulation; alternatively, a bullish divergence on the next price low would be the first reversal clue.

## Volatility & Mean Reversion

- **ATR ($0.40):** Volatility is steady-to-rising; daily range risk is roughly ±$0.40 (~5.4% of price). Position sizing and stops must be wide — a 2×ATR stop implies ~$0.80 of risk per share.
- **Bollinger Bands:** Price ($7.44) is between the middle band ($8.33) and the lower band ($7.22), drifting toward the lower band. Price is not yet at the lower band, so there is room for further downside before a statistical mean-reversion setup triggers. A touch of ~$7.22 combined with RSI <30 would be the highest-probability bounce zone technically.

## Volume & Participation

Volume has dried up considerably — ~5.0M on 10/09 versus 40–140M during October 2025 and the May 2026 spike (141M on 05/12). Declining volume on a decline can signal exhaustion, but it also means rallies lack sponsorship; there is no volume evidence of accumulation.

## Key Levels

- **Support:** $7.34 (10/09 low) → $7.22 (Bollinger lower band) → ~$6.31 (March 2026 low region, outside indicator window — flagged as price-history-based only)
- **Resistance:** $7.94 (10 EMA) → $8.33–8.42 (Bollinger mid / 50 SMA confluence) → $9.10 (200 SMA)

## Actionable Takeaways

- **Bears/trend-followers:** The trend, momentum, and MA stack all align bearish. Rallies into $7.94–$8.42 are lower-high candidates until proven otherwise.
- **Bottom-fishers:** No confirmed reversal signal yet. Watch for (a) RSI <30, (b) a MACD histogram uptick / bullish divergence, and (c) a volume-backed reclaim of the 10 EMA — all three absent today.
- **Risk:** ATR of $0.40 means tight stops will be whipsawed; any long attempt needs ~$0.80 of room or very small sizing.

# QUBT — Fundamental Analysis Report (as of 2026-10-09)

## Scope and data caveats

This report covers Quantum Computing Inc. (QUBT) using SEC EDGAR facts filed on or before 2026-10-09. Two requested feeds were withheld by the vendor for point-in-time integrity: profile/market-cap data (it would leak present-day values into a 2026-10-09 view) and insider transactions (no filing dates available to prove what was public by then). Everything below is based on the filed financial statements only — quarterly balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow.

All figures in USD millions unless noted.

## Company profile

Quantum Computing Inc. is a quantum computing technology company. For most of its history it has been a pre-revenue R&D stage company funded entirely by equity issuance. Only in 2026 did it begin reporting meaningful revenue for the first time, coinciding with a massive expansion of its balance sheet through equity financing. As of 2026-10-09 it remains a speculative, early-commercialization company where the equity raise, not operations, is the dominant financial story.

## Balance sheet — the transformation

Total assets and equity have grown explosively since 2024:

| Period | Total Assets | Cash | Total Liabilities | Stockholders' Equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-12-31 | 79 | 3 | 4 | 68 |
| 2024-12-31 | 154 | 3 | 11 | 107 |
| 2025-03-31 | 243 | 79 | 46 | 221 |
| 2025-06-30 | 426 | 166 | 22 | 396 |
| 2025-09-30 | 898 | 349 | 30 | 878 |
| 2025-12-31 | 1,619 | 352 | 20 | 1,598 |
| 2026-03-31 | 1,621 | 738 | 21 | 1,597 |
| 2026-06-30 | 1,639 | 189 | 47 | 1,592 |

Key observations:

- **Assets grew ~21x from end-2023 ($79M) to mid-2026 ($1,639M).** This is almost entirely financed by shareholder dilution, not profits — equity grew in lockstep.
- **Liquidity peaked at $738M cash on 2026-03-31** and fell sharply to $189M by 2026-06-30 — a ~$549M drawdown in one quarter. Current assets fell from $1,134M to $988M over the same period.
- **The cash drop is investing, not operations.** The cash flow statement shows ~$466M (Q1) and ~$474M (six months) of investing outflow in 2026 — the company moved roughly half a billion dollars out of cash into investments (likely treasuries/marketable securities and/or capital buildout). Traders should note reported "cash and equivalents" understates total liquid resources; current assets of $988M vs cash of $189M implies ~$800M in non-cash current assets, likely short-term investments.
- **Liabilities remain trivial** ($47M at 2026-06-30, of which $19M current). Essentially zero debt; the balance sheet is unlevered and net-asset-heavy.
- The earlier history (2017–2022) shows a company that repeatedly came close to running out of cash — cash fell to ~$0M in 2020 and ~$5–7M in 2022–2024 before the 2024–2025 raise cycle began.

## Income statement — first revenue, still deeply lossmaking

| Period | Revenue | Cost of Revenue | Gross Profit | Operating Income | Net Income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-09-30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -6 | -6 | -0.06 |
| 2025-03-31 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -8 | +17 | +0.11 |
| 2025-06-30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -10 | -36 | -0.26 |
| 2025-09-30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -10 | +2 | +0.01 |
| 2026-03-31 | 4 | 4 | -1 | -21 | -4 | -0.02 |
| 2026-06-30 | 6 | 7 | -1 | -23 | -12 | -0.05 |

Key observations:

- **Revenue appeared for the first time in 2026**: ~$4M in Q1, ~$6M in Q2. Before that, revenue was literally $0 for every reported quarter back to 2022 (the table shows zeros from 2022-09-30 onward, and nothing before).
- **Revenue is loss-making at the gross line**: cost of revenue exceeded revenue in both 2026 quarters (gross profit -$1M each). The initial revenue base is not yet profitable even before opex.
- **Operating losses are widening, not narrowing**: -$21M and -$23M in 2026 H1 vs -$5–10M/quarter in 2025. The company is scaling spend ahead of the revenue ramp.
- **Net income is noisy due to non-operating items.** 2025-03-31 showed +$17M net income and 2025-09-30 +$2M despite operating losses — these quarters presumably included non-cash gains (e.g., warrant/derivative remeasurement or investment gains), and 2025-06-30 showed -$36M. Operating income is the cleaner read: consistently and increasingly negative.
- EPS on a diluted basis is small in absolute terms (-$0.02 to -$0.05 in 2026) largely because the share count ballooned with the equity raises.

## Cash flow — burn rate and the raise cycle

Operating cash flow (quarterly figures are cumulative YTD in the vendor table):

- 2024 full year (9-mo shown): -$12M; Q4 implied ~-4M → roughly -$16M for the year.
- 2025: -$19M through nine months → roughly -$25M+ for the full year.
- 2026: -$9M (Q1) and -$23M (six months) → **run-rate now ~$12–14M per quarter and accelerating**, consistent with the widening operating losses.

Financing:

- The funding cycle is stark: 2025 nine-month financing inflow of **$759M** (94 + 283 tranches visible quarterly), followed by only ~$8M total in 2026 H1. The mega-raise happened in 2025; 2026 is the deployment phase.
- Investing outflow of **~$530M in 2026 H1** — the dominant use of the raised cash.
- Capex is small (~$2–4M/quarter) but rising — $4M in the 2026 six-month figure vs $2–3M in prior periods.

## Financial history summary

- **2017–2021:** near-zero assets, chronic losses, repeated near-insolvency (cash ~$0 in 2020). A -$27M loss quarter in 2018-09 stands out (likely an impairment or one-time charge).
- **2022–2023:** first capital injection cycle (~$90M equity in mid-2022); losses ran ~$5–8M/quarter; cash stayed thin ($2–7M).
- **2024–2025:** the big raise — equity went from ~$70M to ~$1.6B; cash peaked above $350M then $738M after continued inflows into early 2026.
- **2026:** revenue finally appears (still gross-margin negative), operating burn accelerates, and the war chest is being deployed into investments.

## Actionable takeaways for traders

1. **This is a balance-sheet story, not an earnings story.** With ~$988M in current assets, ~$47M in liabilities, and ~$14M/quarter operating burn, the company has years of runway. Bankruptcy/dilution risk is low near-term; the risk is valuation, not solvency.
2. **Watch the revenue ramp quality.** First revenue arrived in 2026 ($4M → $6M QoQ, +50%) but at negative gross margin. If gross margin doesn't turn positive within a few quarters, the revenue is promotional/cost-recovery, not a real business.
3. **The $530M investing deployment in H1 2026 is the key open question** — what it was deployed into (treasuries vs. fab/equipment buildout vs. acquisitions) determines whether this is interest income padding or genuine capacity expansion. Check the next 10-Q investment footnote.
4. **Non-operating items distort EPS.** Ignore headline net income (+$17M in one 2025 quarter with -$8M operating income); use operating income and operating cash flow as the truth metrics.
5. **Dilution is the standing risk.** The entire asset base came from issuing shares. When the next raise comes, it will be large. Current financing inflows have slowed to ~$4M/quarter, so if burn stays ~$15–25M/quarter including capex, expect the next major financing event within ~2–3 years — earlier if investing outflows continue.
6. **No insider-transaction signal available** — the vendor cannot provide a point-in-time filing-date view, so insider buying/selling could not be verified as of 2026-10-09. Do not treat absence of this data as absence of insider activity.

## Key points table

| Category | Finding | Trading relevance |
|---|---|---|
| Balance sheet | $1,639M assets, $1,592M equity, $47M liabilities (2026-06-30) | Solvent, unlevered; value is asset-backed |
| Liquidity | Cash $189M but current assets $988M (2026-06-30) | ~$800M in non-cash current assets (likely ST investments) |
| Revenue | First ever revenue: $4M (Q1'26), $6M (Q2'26) | Early commercialization; watch the ramp |
| Margins | Gross profit -$1M both 2026 quarters | Revenue not yet covering direct costs |
| Operating loss | -$21M / -$23M in 2026 H1, widening | Burn accelerating as company scales |
| Net income | Distorted by non-operating items (+17, -36, +2 in 2025) | Use operating income, not EPS |
| Operating cash burn | ~$12–14M/quarter run rate (2026) | ~5+ years runway at current burn |
| Financing | $759M raised in 2025; only ~$8M in 2026 H1 | Raise cycle done; deployment phase now |
| Investing | ~$530M outflow in 2026 H1 | Where it went is the key due-diligence item |
| Capex | Small but rising (~$2M/quarter) | Not a capital-intensive ramp yet |
| Dilution | Entire $1.6B equity base from share issuance | Next raise is a matter of when, not if |
| Insider data | Not available point-in-time | No signal; verify via Form 4 filings directly |
| Fundamentals risk | Pre-profit, gross-margin negative, valuation-driven | Speculative; position size accordingly |

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for QUBT — Opening Argument

Let me be direct: the bear hasn't spoken yet, so I'll preempt their entire playbook. The bear case writes itself — downtrend, negative gross margin, dilution history, -65% in twelve months. All true. And all, I'd argue, already in the price at $7.44. Here's why the bull side deserves the trade.

## 1. The balance sheet is the moat nobody's pricing

Bears will say "pre-profit spec tech, run." But look at the actual numbers: **$1,639M in total assets, $1,592M in equity, and only $47M in liabilities** as of 2026-06-30. This is an unlevered, asset-backed company with roughly $988M in current assets. Operating burn is ~$12–14M/quarter — that's **years of runway, not months**.

Compare that to where this company was in 2020–2023: chronic near-insolvency, cash under $5M, surviving quarter to quarter. The single biggest historical risk — running out of money and being forced into distressed dilution — has been *eliminated*. The 2025 raise cycle ($759M in nine months) transformed QUBT from a company that begs the market for cash into one that can fund its own commercialization timeline on its own terms. That is a fundamentally different risk profile than the chart suggests.

## 2. First revenue is here, and it's growing 50% QoQ

For a decade QUBT reported literal $0 revenue quarters. In 2026 that changed: $4M in Q1, $6M in Q2 — **+50% sequential growth** on the first revenue base in company history. Yes, gross margin is negative (-$1M/quarter). That's what early photonic-chip/foundry commercialization looks like: you take early orders at cost-recovery pricing to anchor customers, qualify your process, and build reference designs. Every foundry-adjacent semiconductor story goes through this phase. The question isn't whether Q2 margins were negative — it's whether the ramp continues. $4M → $6M says the demand curve exists.

## 3. The technicals the bear will cite are actually capitulation-setting

The technical report is bearish — I'll concede the trend freely. But read it closely:

- **RSI at 32.6** — one session from oversold territory where squeezes are born.
- **Price at $7.44 vs. Bollinger lower band at $7.22** — the report itself flags $7.22 as "the highest-probability bounce zone technically."
- **Volume collapsed to ~5M** from 40–140M during the October 2025 run. The bears read this as "no accumulation." I read it differently: the sellers are *exhausted*. Nobody left to sell is exactly what a bottom looks like before it confirms.
- **The September rally to $9.16** — a +23% move in weeks — proved this stock can move violently when the theme bids. The unwind created the entry, it didn't disprove the thesis.

The bear will call $7.34 "weak support." Fine — but with RSI nearing 30, price at the lower band, and seller volume dried up, the asymmetry at $7.44 is heavily skewed: ~$0.20–0.30 to the capitulation floor versus $0.50 to the 10 EMA, $0.90–1.00 to the 50 SMA confluence, and $1.66 to the 200 SMA on a real squeeze.

## 4. Macro is now a tailwind, not a headwind

- **"Tech rebounds as AI-trade jitters ease"** — QUBT is a leveraged expression of the AI/quantum theme. When the theme catches a bid, QUBT historically out-moves it.
- **Oil down to $103, Iran strike off the table before midterms** — geopolitical risk premium is draining out. Risk-on tape favors high-beta names first.
- Yes, rates are restrictive — the bear's best macro point. But that's been true all year and didn't stop the September +23% rally. QUBT trades on theme beta and catalysts, not duration math.

## 5. Answering the bear's three best arguments before they make them

**"It's just dilution funding losses."** The dilution already happened — it's *in* the share count. The $759M raise is deployed capital now, not future dilution. Current financing inflows are ~$4M/quarter and burn is ~$14M/quarter; the next raise is a 2028+ problem. Near-term, dilution risk is *lower* than it's been in this company's history.

**"Revenue is gross-margin negative."** True — at $10M/year of revenue on a company with $1.6B of assets. If the ramp stalls, that's the kill signal and I'll concede the trade. But revenue only *started* in 2026. Judging a first-year commercial ramp by mature-company margins is how you miss every early-stage semiconductor story.

**"The trend is down."** It is. I'm not arguing to buy the trend — I'm arguing the tape is priced for a company with no catalysts, no cash, and no future, when the filings show a company with a billion-dollar war chest, its first real revenue, and a sector tailwind. Markets are most wrong exactly when the chart is ugliest and the data sources go quiet — which is precisely where we are: zero sentiment signal, zero company news, maximum apathy. Apathy is cheap. Conviction is expensive. I'm buying cheap.

## The bottom line

QUBT at $7.44 offers: asset-backed downside (~$1.6B equity vs. sub-$1B implied equity value), a live revenue ramp growing 50% QoQ, an oversold technical setup with a defined floor at $7.22, and a macro tape rotating risk-on into the exact theme this stock levered-expresses. The bear case is real but fully priced; the bull case has catalysts the market hasn't seen yet.

My framework for the debate: this is a **capitulation-zone accumulation play with a defined invalidation** (sustained break below $7.22 with volume) and multi-layer upside ($7.94 → $8.42 → $9.10). Position small, stops wide — ATR says this thing moves 5% a day — but the risk/reward here is asymmetric in our favor.

Your move, bear.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for QUBT — Rebuttal

Thanks for the setup, bull. You wrote a compelling opening — and conveniently answered your own weakest points before I could press them. Let me press them anyway, because a few of your "concessions" are doing a lot of quiet work.

## 1. "Priced in" is doing all the heavy lifting

Your entire thesis rests on the claim that -65% in twelve months means the bad news is priced. That assumes the market was *wrong* on the way down rather than *right*. The chart tells a different story: a full bearish stack (price below a falling 10 EMA, 50 SMA, and 200 SMA), MACD negative and expanding, each price low matched by a lower MACD — **no divergence**. The technical report you cite says explicitly there is no confirmed reversal signal: not RSI <30, not a histogram uptick, not a volume-backed reclaim of the 10 EMA. You're not describing a bottom. You're describing a falling knife and calling the handle a floor.

And the "$7.22 capitulation floor" — that's 3% away on a stock with 5.4% daily ATR. Your "defined invalidation" is inside one normal day's range. That's not a floor; that's a coin flip with extra steps. Below $7.22, the next support the report names is ~$6.31 — another 15% down. Your asymmetry math ($0.22 risk vs $1.66 reward) quietly assumes $7.22 holds. If it doesn't — and nothing in the data says it will — the real downside is -15%+ while the upside requires reclaiming three layers of overhead supply that every prior bounce has failed at.

## 2. The "moat" is a pile of cash bought with your shares

Let's be honest about what $1.6B in equity actually is: it's not a moat, it's a *dilution receipt*. Every dollar of that balance sheet came from printing shares. The company didn't earn a fortress — it sold one. And the deployment is already ugly: **cash fell from $738M to $189M in a single quarter**, with ~$530M of investing outflow in H1 2026 that the fundamentals report itself flags as "the key open question." You call it a war chest being deployed; I call it half a billion dollars leaving the building with no disclosed return. Until we know where it went — treasuries, fab buildout, or something worse — treating it as downside protection is faith, not analysis.

You also claim the next raise is "a 2028+ problem." The report says burn is *accelerating* — operating loss went from -$10M/quarter in 2025 to -$23M in Q2 2026, more than doubling in a year. If that trajectory holds, your runway math is obsolete by the time the next 10-Q prints. This company has survived its entire existence on serial dilution, and its history (near-zero cash in 2020, $5-7M in 2022-24) shows exactly what it does when the market won't fund it. The next raise isn't distant — it's the business model.

## 3. "+50% QoQ revenue growth" is a rounding error with a growth rate

$4M to $6M is a $2M quarter-over-quarter increase on a company carrying $1.6B in assets and burning $23M per quarter. Annualized, that's ~$20-24M of revenue against ~$90M+ of annual operating loss — and **negative gross margin**, meaning every dollar of that revenue *costs money to produce*. You're not describing a demand curve; you're describing two data points, both of which lose money before opex even enters the picture. "Every semiconductor story goes through this phase" — yes, and most of them fail in it. Survivorship bias isn't a thesis.

Your own kill signal — "if the ramp stalls, I concede" — deserves a mirror: if gross margin is still negative after two more quarters, the revenue isn't a business, it's a subsidy to whoever's buying. We're two quarters in and there's no evidence the trend flips.

## 4. Your macro tailwind is a theme basket, not a catalyst

"QUBT is a leveraged expression of the AI/quantum theme" — I'll agree, and that's the bear case in one sentence. A leveraged expression of a theme has no intrinsic floor; when the theme sells, it sells *harder*. You cite the September +23% rally as proof of what it can do — I cite the complete unwind of that rally in under three weeks as proof of what it *does*. Rallies without sponsorship fade, and the volume data confirms it: 5M shares on 10/09 versus 40-140M on real moves. You read that as seller exhaustion. The technical report reads it correctly: no accumulation, no sponsorship, rallies have nothing behind them.

Meanwhile the restrictive-rate backdrop you wave away is precisely the regime that punishes pre-profit, story-driven names with no earnings to anchor valuation. "Rates didn't stop the September rally" — they also didn't stop the 65% decline that preceded and followed it. You're cherry-picking the bounce inside a year-long liquidation.

## 5. The data you don't have is worse than the data you do

Three separate feeds — sentiment, news, company-specific items — returned **zero data** for this window. You spin that as "maximum apathy is cheap." I read it differently: you are constructing a conviction thesis on a stock where the sentiment signal is literally unmeasurable (5.0/10 = "absence of signal," not neutrality), the company news feed has a coverage gap, and insider transactions are unavailable point-in-time — on a name with a *history of volatility around capital raises*. The risk here isn't apathy. It's that you're flying blind into a ticker whose single most dangerous recurring event — a dilutive offering — cannot be ruled out by any data in front of us.

## The bottom line

Your case needs all of the following to be true simultaneously: $7.22 holds despite no technical confirmation, the $530M deployment turns out benign, revenue doubles again while gross margin flips positive, the AI theme keeps bidding, and no offering hits before "2028+." My case needs one thing: the trend that's been in force for twelve months continues — which is what unconfirmed trends usually do.

This is not a capitulation-zone accumulation play. It's a gross-margin-negative, accelerating-burn, single-catalyst-dependent spec name in a confirmed downtrend on every timeframe, being bought on the theory that a 3% support level inside one day's volatility will hold. The risk/reward isn't asymmetric in your favor — it's asymmetric against anyone who can't see the next real support at ~$6.31.
